title: Developer Journey Maps & Targeted Quickstart Program
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview:
This initiative creates a repeatable, data-driven program that maps developer journeys across SDKs, docs, and quickstarts, and launches a targeted quickstart product line to reduce time-to-first-success and increase feature adoption. The goal is to convert new signups into active API callers within 24 hours and improve 30-day retention for DX cohorts by 20% relative to the current baseline.

Why now:
- Activation funnels show strong dropoff between signup and first API call (current median = 3.2 days).
- Teams building integrations need clearer, shorter path to success (sample apps + curated quickstarts).
- Tactical improvements (in-SDK telemetry, guided journey flows) can unlock measurable revenue via higher usage and stickiness.

Goals / OKRs (Q2 2025):
- Objective: Reduce time-to-first-API-call for new devs to <= 24 hours.
  - KR1: 50% of new signups complete a quickstart within 24 hours.
  - KR2: Starter sample apps downloads increase 3x for tracked cohorts.
- Objective: Improve 30-day active retention by 20% for cohorts using the new quickstarts.
  - KR3: 30-day active rate for quickstart cohort >= baseline * 1.20.
  - KR4: NPS for quickstart flow >= +35 (post-completion survey).

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Journey mapping: instrument segments (JS, Python, Go) and map top 5 persona flows (prototype, POC, integration, embed, analytics). Deliverable: journey map artifacts and prioritized friction list.
2) Quickstart program: 6 modular quickstarts (Getting started, Embeddings, Chat, Streaming, Vector Search, Governance patterns) with language-specific code snippets and runnable sample apps.
3) SDK onboarding enhancements: inline quickstart TOC inside SDK README, automated example runner (one-command local run), and error-first UX guidance.
4) Telemetry & dashboards: event schema, activation funnel in console, per-quickstart completion rates, and cohort analysis.
5) Content & enablement: Figma templates, video walkthroughs (2–4 min), localized cheat-sheets.

Approach / Plan:
- Phase 0 (Feb 2025): Kickoff, stakeholder alignment, measurement design, instrumentation spec.
- Phase 1 (Mar 2025): Build sample apps + three pilot quickstarts (JS, Python) and the first funnel dashboard.
- Phase 2 (Apr–May 2025): Expand to remaining quickstarts and languages, integrate SDK README flows, run A/B experiments on quickstart entry copy.
- Phase 3 (Jun 2025): Beta release to selected cohort of 50 customers, iterate, and GA.

Success metrics and tracking:
- Primary metrics: percent of new signups that complete a quickstart within 24 hours; median time-to-first-API-call; 30-day retention of quickstart cohort.
- Signal KPIs: quickstart completion rate by language, runtime errors encountered during quickstarts, sample app repo clones/stars, and API token churn.
- Dashboards: funnel overview in Console (per-release), cohort comparison, and experiment telemetry for A/B tests.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Engineering bandwidth conflict with runtime-1.18 rollout. Mitigation: schedule SDK work into dedicated sprint lane and de-scope non-critical languages for MVP.
- Risk: Telemetry privacy/PII concerns. Mitigation: instrument only event-level signals (no request bodies), coordinate with Security for schema review.
- Risk: Quickstart complexity causing developer frustration. Mitigation: enforce 1-command run and run user testing with 8 external devs in March.

Dependencies:
- ENG-21045: SDK tracing + telemetry hooks (blocking for dashboards).
- DES-981: Design templates and microcopy for quickstart flows.
- PM-33109: Alignment with SDK activation playbooks and existing cohort experiments.

Rollout & Communication:
- Week-of launch plan for Beta cohort: invite list, in-console banner, onboarding email sequence, Slack outreach.
- Training: Solutions Engineering playbook, internal demo, standing office hours for first 2 weeks.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finalize instrumentation spec and event names (owner: Liam Carter).
- Design review for pilot quickstarts (owner: Maya Ruiz, DES-981).
- Kick off ENG spike for one-command sample app runner (owner: Rahul Singh, ENG-21045).
